messages.subject: meaning of summary parameters
parts:
Hi everyone,

coming more from the IRT-world than from CFA, my question is how to interpret those loadings given by the summary function of a mirt-object. Are those like correlations, similar to loadings in a ml-cfa in lavaan?

and are you aware of any reference where the zone between IRT and CFA is explained in a not too technical-mathematical way?

best, felix

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: meaning of summary parameters
parts:
Hi Felix,

The results of summary() are indeed standardized factor loadings like
the kind you would see in lavaan for exploratory and confirmatory item
factor analysis, and are transformed versions of the raw coefficients
returned from coef(). I don't know of any really non-technical talk of
the relationship, but Bock and Aitkin's 1982 seminal estimation
article showed the mathematical relationship to non-linear factor
analysis and how to obtain these coefficients (pp. 455-456). Probably
the best place to get a good grasp of what exactly MIRT models are and
how they relate to factor analysis can be found in Mark Reckase's 2009
book on the topic, which I think is still the best to date. Hope that
helps.

Phil

messages.subject: Re: meaning of summary parameters

A second not-too-technical description on the relationship between FA and IRT would be Wirth & Edwards (2007) Item Factor Analysis in Psychological Methods. It has a brief discussion on the relationship between the two frameworks and the conversion formulas for the 2PL to FA loadings. Its not as comprehensive, but a nice easy read.

Aaron
